name: /sdd:brainstorm: classifies, asks one question, and writes no document
prompt: /sdd:brainstorm let readers subscribe to a widget and get notified when it changes

graders.why: step 1 requires the level and the reason to be said out loud before anything is asked. Deciding silently is how a one-line fix acquires a design document and a new subsystem acquires none, and saying it is what lets the user overrule it
a dialogue command that proposes without asking has skipped its whole purpose. This request is deliberately underspecified: transport, delivery guarantees and who may subscribe are all open

three or more questions in one turn is the failure the one-per-turn rule exists for: answered together they are optimised against each other in a single breath, and the questions worth asking second never get asked. Two is tolerated as a compound sentence; three is a questionnaire
graders.violating_example: What transport? Should it be push or pull? And who can subscribe?

graders.why: this command hands an approved design to /sdd:plan or /sdd:generate-specs and never produces the durable document itself. A dialogue command emitting its own format produces a one-shot briefing with no status header, no dates and no progress log, and then two documents disagree about the same work
graders.violating_example: I have created the plan at .specs/docs/plans/2026-09-22-subscriptions.md

graders.why: the approval gate sits before implementation at every level. A session that designs and implements in the same turn has removed the only review its own design was going to get
graders.violating_example: I've implemented the subscription model in src/subscriptions.py

graders.must_not_match: (?i)(who are the stakeholders|what.{0,5}s the (estimated )?timeline|rollback strategy|priority level)
graders.why: same reason as /sdd:plan: those have an answer for every project, which is why they are worthless, and they spend the five-question budget before reaching what this request actually left open
